newsitem.title: USA: Chronicle says Jobs declines Apple posts.
newsitem.headline: Chronicle says Jobs declines Apple posts.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. co-founder and adviser Steve Jobs has told employees of his Pixar film animation company he has declined the posts of chief executive and chairman of apple, a newspaper reported.
The San Francisco Chronicle, reported on its front page Wednesday that Apple Computer planned to name Jobs as chairman.

The Chronicle quoted from an electronic mail message it said Jobs, who is chief executive of Pixar, sent to employees of the company, saying he had twice declined offers from the Apple board, first to be CEO, then chairman.

"About three weeks ago, the board of directors of Apple told me they were cutting (former Apple Chairman and CEO) Gil Amelio loose. They asked me to be the CEO. I declined," Jobs was quoted as writing in the e-mail.
"Then they asked me to be the chairman. Again I declined," it said. "I love my job at Pixar.... Don't pay any attention to the crazy rumors. That's all they are."
"I have no plans to leave Pixar," the memo concluded, according to the Chronicle.

Several news organizations -- including the Chronicle, CNBC, San Jose Mercury News and Macworld -- had reported in recent days that Apple planned to announce Jobs' appointment as chairman at next week's Macworld trade show in Boston.
The annual convention comes four weeks after Apple ousted Amelio and began its search for a new executive.

Jobs is due to give a keynote address at the show next Wednesday, and the company's effort to entice him back to a top position at Apple was viewed as a bid to tap his extraordinary popularity among Apple Macintosh fans to revive the brand.
